title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Kenya: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Kenya: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step serious and terminal illness checklist for Kenya: palliative care coordination, advance directives, powers of attorney, disability and caregiver support, and estate preparation.
introHtml: Planning medical, legal, and financial matters in Kenya while navigating a serious or terminal illness requires coordinating public health benefits, palliative services, incapacity and succession instruments, social security disability entitlements, and cross-border authentication. Note that this guide uses the verified eCitizen portal of the State Department for Foreign Affairs (mfa.ecitizen.go.ke without altered third-party pages) alongside live portals of the Social Health Authority, Ministry of Health, Lands, NSSF, NCPWD, KEHPCA, Kenya Law, and the Hague Conference (HCCH).

steps.title: Healthcare Financing, Palliative Support, and Medical Assessment
steps.html:
• Verify benefit entitlements and facility coverage under the Social Health Authority (SHA), which administers the Primary Healthcare Fund and Social Health Insurance Fund (SHIF) packages, including chronic condition management and listed palliative and end-of-life care tariffs [1][2].
  • Locate specialized hospice or home-based palliative teams nationwide through the provider directory maintained by the Kenya Hospices and Palliative Care Association (KEHPCA) [7][8].
  • If progressive illness limits work or daily living, arrange an official disability evaluation through the Ministry of Health using the Progressive Chronic Disorders assessment protocol (Form REFMOH-276G), and apply for registration with the National Council for Persons with Disabilities (NCPWD) to unlock statutory protections and tax or fee exemptions [6][9].

steps.title: Powers of Attorney, Capacity Safeguards, and Will Execution
steps.html:
• Execute and formally register a Power of Attorney through the State Department for Lands and Physical Planning at Ardhi House (registration charge Kshs. 1,000; requires the executed instrument, proof of stamp duty payment, national ID or passport, KRA PIN certificate, and two passport photographs) under the Registration of Documents Act (Cap. 285) while decision-making capacity is intact [5][13].
  • Address cognitive or neurological incapacity safeguards early under the Mental Health Act (Cap. 248), which governs court appointment of managers for the estate and personal care of persons unable to manage their own affairs [12].
  • Draft and sign a valid will under the Law of Succession Act (Cap. 160), which requires a written will to be signed by the testator and attested by two or more competent witnesses present together [11].

steps.title: NSSF Invalidity Benefits and Beneficiary Nominations
steps.html:
• Review eligibility for an Invalidity Benefit with the National Social Security Fund (NSSF) under the National Social Security Fund Act (No. 45 of 2013), which compensates contributing members certified by a medical board as permanently incapable of regular gainful employment [3][14].
  • Update NSSF beneficiary and next-of-kin details alongside occupational pension, Sacco, and life-policy nominations so dependants match current family arrangements [3][4].

steps.title: Financial, Tax, and Property Record Preparation
steps.html:
• Consolidate National ID or passport copies, KRA PIN certificates, title deeds, bank details, SHIF and NSSF statements, and certified copies of marriage or birth records [1][3][5].
  • Keep original wills and Power of Attorney registration receipts in a secure, known location accessible to the appointed executor or agent [5][11].

steps.title: Cross-Border Document Authentication (Non-Apostille)
steps.html:
• Kenya is not a Contracting Party to the HCCH 1961 Hague Apostille Convention, so Apostilles are not issued or accepted as standalone authentication; foreign-bound documents require consular legalization [15].
  • Submit Kenyan medical certificates and reports, notarized powers of attorney, or civil status certificates online for authentication and legalization through the State Department for Foreign Affairs eCitizen portal before seeking attestation at the destination state's embassy or high commission [10].
